Definition: middle voice from G1223 and G5087; to put apart, i.e. (figuratively) dispose (by assignment, compact, or bequest):--appoint, make, testator.
BiblicalUsage: To make a covenant is to settle it by a promise, and the word is used of God making His covenant with His people. He appoints a kingdom to His disciples, He makes a covenant with the house of Israel, and a testament is of force only after the death of the one who made it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the covenant is made sure by death. A will means nothing until the testator dies, and the new covenant stands because Christ died to make it stand, which is why it cannot be broken.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
